children: , the networking and cybersecurity company, pushed Splunk AI deeper into private-cloud, on-premises and air-gapped environments, targeting enterprises that cannot simply send sensitive machine data into public AI systems. Shares gained approximately 0.2% to $109.73, based on the latest quoted price.

The available AI POD packages Cisco infrastructure with Nvidia accelerated computing and Kubernetes software, giving customers a more controlled path to deploy AI workloads behind their own security boundaries. Splunk AI Assistant is already available, while Agent Launchpad is expected later this year. Cisco is also adding Tokenomics capabilities designed to track agent spending, attribute usage and forecast consumptionan increasingly important problem as companies move from small AI experiments toward fleets of autonomous agents.

That combination gives Cisco two shots at the enterprise AI budget: the infrastructure running the workloads and the governance layer controlling what those workloads cost. But the valuation leaves less room for execution misses. The chart puts Cisco at $109.73 versus a GF Value estimate of $74.62, meaning the stock trades 47.05% above GF Value. With Cisco yet to disclose pricing or committed deployment volumes for these products, investors are already paying a sizable premium for growth that still needs to show up in adoption and revenue.

title: Cisco Moves Higher as Splunk Takes Agents Behind the Firewall
